title: Percent Problems
seo_title: Grade 7 Percent Problems Worksheets: Percent Change, Discounts, Tax, Tips and Simple Interest
standard_text: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems. Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 percent problems worksheets: percent of a number, percent increase and decrease, discounts and markups, sales tax, tips, commission, simple interest and percent error. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_sub: For percent change, divide the change by the original amount. A discount subtracts, tax and markups add.
body_html:
Percent means out of 100

Change the percent to a decimal: 25% = 0.25, 6% = 0.06, 150% = 1.5. Then multiply. Percent of means times.

ProblemRuleExample
Percent of a numberpart = percent × whole25% of 80 = 0.25 × 80 = 20
Percent changechange ÷ original40 to 50: 10 ÷ 40 = 25%
Discountprice × (1 − rate)$80, 25% off: 80 × 0.75 = $60
Tax or markupprice × (1 + rate)$40, 6% tax: 40 × 1.06 = $42.40
Simple interestI = P × r × t$500, 4%, 3 years: $60

Percent change

Find the change, then divide by the original amount. Percent error works the same way, but you divide by the actual value.

Example

A $64 pair of shoes is 15% off. What is the sale price?

Discount: 0.15 × 64 = $9.60.

Sale price: $64 − $9.60 = $54.40.

Or in one step: 64 × 0.85 = $54.40.

Answer: $54.40

Example

A price goes from $40 to $50. What is the percent increase?

Change: 50 − 40 = 10.

Divide by the original: 10 ÷ 40 = 0.25.

Answer: 25%

Common mistakes

  • Stopping at the discount: 25% off $80 is $60, not $20.
  • Dividing by the new amount: 40 to 50 is a 25% increase, not 20%.
  • Subtracting the percent as a number: 25% off $80 is not $80 − 25.
  • Writing 5% as 0.5: 5% = 0.05.

faq.q: How do you find a percent of a number?
faq.a: Change the percent to a decimal and multiply. 15% of 120 = 0.15 × 120 = 18.

faq.q: How do you find percent increase or decrease?
faq.a: Subtract to find the change, then divide by the original amount and multiply by 100. From 80 to 60: 20 ÷ 80 = 0.25, a 25% decrease.

faq.q: How do I find a sale price?
faq.a: Find the discount and subtract it, or multiply by what is left. 25% off $80: $80 × 0.75 = $60.
Interest that is a fixed percent of the starting amount each year: I = P × r × t. $500 at 4% for 3 years earns 500 × 0.04 × 3 = $60.

items.q: What is 25% of 80?
What is 10% of 340?
What is 5% of 60?
What is 40% of 75?
What is 15% of 120?
What is 150% of 40?
items.e: 150% means 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5. 1.5 × 40 = 60. More than 100% gives more than the whole.

items.q: What is 8% of 250?
What is 120% of 35?
items.e: 120% means 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2. 1.2 × 35 = 42. More than 100% gives more than the whole.

items.q: What is 2.5% of 400?
What is 0.5% of 600?
What is 35% of 180?
What is 200% of 14?
items.e: 200% means 200 ÷ 100 = 2. 2 × 14 = 28. More than 100% gives more than the whole.

items.q: 18 is what percent of 72?
items.e: Percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 18 ÷ 72 × 100 = 25%. Not 400%: that divides the whole by the part.

items.q: 45 is what percent of 60?
items.e: Percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 45 ÷ 60 × 100 = 75%.

items.q: 7 is what percent of 20?
items.e: Percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 7 ÷ 20 × 100 = 35%.

items.q: 90 is what percent of 60?
items.e: Percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 90 ÷ 60 × 100 = 150%.

items.q: 3 is what percent of 150?
items.e: Percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 3 ÷ 150 × 100 = 2%. Not 5,000%: that divides the whole by the part.

items.q: 27 is what percent of 36?
items.e: Percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 27 ÷ 36 × 100 = 75%.

items.q: 12 is 30% of what number?
items.e: 30% of the number is 12, so the number is 12 ÷ 0.3 = 40.

items.q: 45 is 75% of what number?
items.e: 75% of the number is 45, so the number is 45 ÷ 0.75 = 60.

items.q: A value changes from 40 to 50. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 50 − 40 = 10. Percent increase = change ÷ original = 10 ÷ 40 = 25%. Not 20%: divide by the original amount, 40, not the new amount.

items.q: A value changes from 80 to 60. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 80 − 60 = 20. Percent decrease = change ÷ original = 20 ÷ 80 = 25%.

items.q: A value changes from 25 to 35. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 35 − 25 = 10. Percent increase = change ÷ original = 10 ÷ 25 = 40%.

items.q: A value changes from 200 to 150. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 200 − 150 = 50. Percent decrease = change ÷ original = 50 ÷ 200 = 25%.

items.q: A value changes from 50 to 80. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 80 − 50 = 30. Percent increase = change ÷ original = 30 ÷ 50 = 60%. Not 37.5%: divide by the original amount, 50, not the new amount.

items.q: A value changes from 120 to 90. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 120 − 90 = 30. Percent decrease = change ÷ original = 30 ÷ 120 = 25%.

items.q: A value changes from 16 to 20. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 20 − 16 = 4. Percent increase = change ÷ original = 4 ÷ 16 = 25%. Not 20%: divide by the original amount, 16, not the new amount.

items.q: A value changes from 75 to 60. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 75 − 60 = 15. Percent decrease = change ÷ original = 15 ÷ 75 = 20%. Not 25%: divide by the original amount, 75, not the new amount.

items.q: A value changes from 30 to 54. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 54 − 30 = 24. Percent increase = change ÷ original = 24 ÷ 30 = 80%.

items.q: A value changes from 250 to 200. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 250 − 200 = 50. Percent decrease = change ÷ original = 50 ÷ 250 = 20%. Not 25%: divide by the original amount, 250, not the new amount.

items.q: Increase 60 by 20%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 20% of 60 is 12. Add it: 60 + 12 = 72. Or multiply by 1.2.

items.q: Decrease 80 by 25%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 25% of 80 is 20. Subtract it: 80 − 20 = 60. Or multiply by 0.75.

items.q: Increase 150 by 10%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 10% of 150 is 15. Add it: 150 + 15 = 165. Or multiply by 1.1.

items.q: Decrease 45 by 40%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 40% of 45 is 18. Subtract it: 45 − 18 = 27. Or multiply by 0.6.

items.q: Increase 240 by 15%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 15% of 240 is 36. Add it: 240 + 36 = 276. Or multiply by 1.15.

items.q: Decrease 90 by 50%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 50% of 90 is 45. Subtract it: 90 − 45 = 45. Or multiply by 0.5.

items.q: Increase 36 by 125%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 125% of 36 is 45. Add it: 36 + 45 = 81. Or multiply by 2.25.

items.q: Decrease 500 by 8%. What is the new amount?
items.e: 8% of 500 is 40. Subtract it: 500 − 40 = 460. Or multiply by 0.92.

items.q: Which number do you multiply by to increase an amount by 30%?
items.e: An increase of 30% leaves 130% of the amount: 1.3.

items.q: Which number do you multiply by to decrease an amount by 15%?
items.e: An decrease of 15% leaves 85% of the amount: 0.85.

items.q: A jacket costs $80. It is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 25% of $80 = $20. Sale price = $80 − $20 = $60. Not $20: that is only the discount.

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $64. It is on sale for 15% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 15% of $64 = $9.60. Sale price = $64 − $9.60 = $54.40. Not $9.60: that is only the discount.

items.q: A video game costs $59. It is on sale for 20% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 20% of $59 = $11.80. Sale price = $59 − $11.80 = $47.20. Not $11.80: that is only the discount.

items.q: A backpack costs $45. It is on sale for 30% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 30% of $45 = $13.50. Sale price = $45 − $13.50 = $31.50. Not $13.50: that is only the discount.

items.q: A bike costs $240. It is on sale for 35% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 35% of $240 = $84. Sale price = $240 − $84 = $156. Not $84: that is only the discount.

items.q: A lamp costs $38. It is on sale for 40% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 40% of $38 = $15.20. Sale price = $38 − $15.20 = $22.80. Not $15.20: that is only the discount.

items.q: A tablet costs $320. It is on sale for 12% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount = 12% of $320 = $38.40. Sale price = $320 − $38.40 = $281.60. Not $38.40: that is only the discount.

items.q: A store buys a T-shirt for $12 and marks it up 50%. What is the selling price?
A store buys a phone case for $8 and marks it up 75%. What is the selling price?
A store buys a chair for $60 and marks it up 40%. What is the selling price?
A store buys a box of pens for $4 and marks it up 125%. What is the selling price?
A store buys a snack for $2.50 and marks it up 60%. What is the selling price?
A shirt was $50 and is now $40. What percent is the discount?
A shirt was $120 and is now $84. What percent is the discount?
A shirt was $75 and is now $60. What percent is the discount?
A shirt was $36 and is now $27. What percent is the discount?
A $100 coat is 20% off. Then you take another 10% off the sale price. What do you pay?
items.e: 20% off $100 is $80. 10% of $80 is $8, so you pay $80 − $8 = $72. Not $70: the second discount is on $80, not $100.

items.q: A $40 game is 25% off, and the store adds 25% to the sale price later. What is the final price?
items.e: 25% off $40 is $30. 25% of $30 is $7.50, so the price is $37.50. Not $40: the two 25%s are of different amounts.

items.q: Which is the better deal on a $60 item?
A store has 40% off everything. A $55 sweater becomes how much?
An item costs $40. The sales tax is 6%. What is the total cost?
items.e: Tax = 6% of $40 = $2.40. Total = $40 + $2.40 = $42.40. Not $2.40: that is the tax only.

items.q: An item costs $25. The sales tax is 8%. What is the total cost?
items.e: Tax = 8% of $25 = $2. Total = $25 + $2 = $27. Not $2: that is the tax only.

items.q: An item costs $120. The sales tax is 7%. What is the total cost?
items.e: Tax = 7% of $120 = $8.40. Total = $120 + $8.40 = $128.40. Not $8.40: that is the tax only.

items.q: An item costs $64. The sales tax is 7.5%. What is the total cost?
items.e: Tax = 7.5% of $64 = $4.80. Total = $64 + $4.80 = $68.80. Not $4.80: that is the tax only.

items.q: An item costs $15. The sales tax is 5%. What is the total cost?
items.e: Tax = 5% of $15 = $0.75. Total = $15 + $0.75 = $15.75. Not $0.75: that is the tax only.

items.q: An item costs $250. The sales tax is 4%. What is the total cost?
items.e: Tax = 4% of $250 = $10. Total = $250 + $10 = $260. Not $10: that is the tax only.

items.q: A meal costs $40. How much is a 15% tip?
A meal costs $64. How much is a 20% tip?
A meal costs $28. How much is an 18% tip?
A meal costs $85. How much is a 20% tip?
A meal costs $52. How much is a 15% tip?
A salesperson earns 5% commission. She sells $2,000 of goods. How much commission does she earn?
A salesperson earns 8% commission. She sells $850 of goods. How much commission does she earn?
A salesperson earns 3% commission. She sells $12,000 of goods. How much commission does she earn?
You put $500 in an account that pays 4% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 3 years?
items.e: Simple interest I = P × r × t = $500 × 0.04 × 3 = $60. Not $560: that is the total in the account, not just the interest.

items.q: You put $1,200 in an account that pays 5% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 2 years?
items.e: Simple interest I = P × r × t = $1,200 × 0.05 × 2 = $120. Not $1,320: that is the total in the account, not just the interest.

items.q: You put $800 in an account that pays 2.5% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 4 years?
items.e: Simple interest I = P × r × t = $800 × 0.025 × 4 = $80. Not $880: that is the total in the account, not just the interest.

items.q: You put $2,000 in an account that pays 6% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 1.5 years?
items.e: Simple interest I = P × r × t = $2,000 × 0.06 × 1.5 = $180. Not $2,180: that is the total in the account, not just the interest.

items.q: You put $350 in an account that pays 3% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 5 years?
items.e: Simple interest I = P × r × t = $350 × 0.03 × 5 = $52.50. Not $402.50: that is the total in the account, not just the interest.

items.q: You put $1,500 in an account that pays 2% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 6 years?
items.e: Simple interest I = P × r × t = $1,500 × 0.02 × 6 = $180. Not $1,680: that is the total in the account, not just the interest.

items.q: Emma guessed there were 40 marbles in a jar. There were 50. What was her percent error?
items.e: Error = 50 − 40 = 10. Percent error = 10 ÷ 50 (the actual value) = 0.2 = 20%. Not 25%: divide by the actual value, not the guess.

items.q: A board should be 2.5 m long. It was cut to 2.4 m. What is the percent error?
A town's population grew from 8,000 to 9,200. What was the percent increase?
A shirt is on sale for $24 after a 20% discount. What was the original price?
items.e: The sale price is 80% of the original, so the original is $24 ÷ 0.8 = $30. Not $28.80: adding 20% of $24 uses the wrong base.

items.q: After 8% tax, a total bill is $54. What was the price before tax?
items.e: The total is 108% of the price: $54 ÷ 1.08 = $50.

items.q: A family's dinner costs $72. They leave an 18% tip. What is the total they pay?
A store pays $30 for a game and sells it for $45. What percent is the markup?
items.e: Markup = $15. 15 ÷ 30 (the store's cost) = 0.5 = 50%. Not 33.33%: divide by the cost, not the selling price.

items.q: A $90 pair of jeans is 30% off, and then 6% tax is added to the sale price. What is the final cost?
Eli's pay rose from $15 to $16.80 an hour. What was the percent raise?
A $250 bike loses 20% of its value each year. What is it worth after 1 year?
In a class of 32 students, 75% ride the bus. How many students ride the bus?
A basketball player made 18 of 24 free throws. What percent did she make?
A $2,400 loan has 5% simple interest per year. How much is owed in total after 3 years?
items.e: I = 2,400 × 0.05 × 3 = $360. Total = $2,400 + $360 = $2,760. Not $360: that is only the interest.

items.q: A real estate agent earns 3% commission on a $280,000 house. How much does the agent earn?
A water bill went from $60 to $48. What was the percent decrease?
items.e: Decrease = $12. 12 ÷ 60 = 0.2 = 20%. Not 25%: divide by the original $60, not $48.

items.q: A recipe needs 400 g of flour. Mia uses 10% more. How much flour does she use?
A phone's battery is at 80%. It loses 15% of the full charge. What percent is left?
items.e: 15% of the full charge is 15 percentage points: 80% − 15% = 65%.

items.q: A store marks up a $40 jacket by 50%. Later it is sold at 50% off. What is the final price?
A savings account pays 4% simple interest. How many years does it take $500 to earn $100?
items.e: Interest each year = 4% of $500 = $20. $100 ÷ $20 = 5 years.

items.q: A city's bus fare went from $2.50 to $3.00. What was the percent increase?
items.e: Increase = $0.50. 0.50 ÷ 2.50 = 0.2 = 20%. Not 16.67%: divide by the old fare.
